label: Language & Communication
scope_note: Human languages — their structure, history and writing systems — and the media through which people communicate.

label: Linguistics
scope_note: The scientific study of language.

label: Phonetics and phonology
scope_note: Speech sounds and the sound systems of languages, including the handshapes and movements of sign languages.

label: Grammar
scope_note: How words are formed and combined into sentences.

label: Semantics and pragmatics
scope_note: Meaning in language, and how context shapes it.

label: Historical linguistics
scope_note: How languages change over time and how their relationships are reconstructed.

label: Sociolinguistics
scope_note: Language in society: dialects, multilingualism, language policy and language and identity.

label: Psycholinguistics
scope_note: How language is learned, produced and understood.

label: Computational linguistics
scope_note: Computational models of language and language technology.

label: Language documentation and endangerment
scope_note: Recording and revitalizing languages, many of which are endangered.

label: Names and naming
scope_note: Personal names, place names and naming practices across cultures.

label: Lexicography
scope_note: Compiling and studying dictionaries.

label: Languages of the world
scope_note: The world's roughly seven thousand languages, grouped by family where relationships are established; regional groupings are marked as such.

label: Afroasiatic languages
scope_note: Language family of North Africa, the Horn of Africa and West Asia, including Arabic, Amharic, Hausa, Hebrew, Somali and Berber languages.

label: Austroasiatic languages
scope_note: Language family of mainland Southeast Asia and parts of South Asia, including Vietnamese, Khmer and Santali.

label: Austronesian languages
scope_note: Language family spread from Madagascar to Rapa Nui, including Malay-Indonesian, Tagalog, Malagasy, Māori and Hawaiian.

label: Dravidian languages
scope_note: Language family of southern India and Sri Lanka, including Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.

label: Indo-European languages
scope_note: Language family of Europe, Iran and much of South Asia, including Hindi-Urdu, Bengali, Persian, Russian, Spanish, English and Greek.

label: Japonic languages
scope_note: Japanese and the Ryukyuan languages.

label: Koreanic languages
scope_note: Korean and the Jeju language.

label: Kra–Dai languages
scope_note: Language family of mainland Southeast Asia and southern China, including Thai and Lao.

label: Mongolic languages
scope_note: Mongolian and related languages of Central and East Asia.

label: Niger–Congo languages
scope_note: The largest language family by number of languages, spread across sub-Saharan Africa, including Yoruba, Igbo, Swahili, Zulu and Wolof; the extent of the family is debated.

label: Nilo-Saharan languages
scope_note: A proposed family of African languages, including Kanuri, Luo, Maasai and Songhay; its unity is debated among linguists.

label: Sino-Tibetan languages
scope_note: Language family including the Chinese languages, Tibetan, Burmese and many languages of the Himalayas.

label: Trans–New Guinea languages
scope_note: The largest of the language families of New Guinea and nearby islands.

label: Tungusic languages
scope_note: Languages of Siberia and northeast China, including Evenki and Manchu.

label: Turkic languages
scope_note: Language family stretching from southeastern Europe to Siberia, including Turkish, Azerbaijani, Uzbek, Kazakh, Uyghur and Tatar.

label: Uralic languages
scope_note: Language family including Finnish, Estonian, Hungarian and the Sami and Samoyedic languages.

label: Languages of the Caucasus (regional grouping)
scope_note: The Kartvelian, Northwest Caucasian and Northeast Caucasian families, grouped here by region rather than by descent.

label: Khoisan languages (regional grouping)
scope_note: Click languages of southern and eastern Africa belonging to several families, grouped here by region rather than by descent.

label: Aboriginal Australian languages (regional grouping)
scope_note: The Pama–Nyungan family and several other families of Aboriginal Australia, grouped here by region.

label: Indigenous languages of the Americas (regional grouping)
scope_note: Many families and isolates, among them Quechuan, Mayan, Uto-Aztecan, Tupian, Arawakan and Algonquian, grouped here by region rather than by descent.

label: Language isolates
scope_note: Languages with no demonstrated relatives, such as Basque, Ainu and Burushaski.

label: Sign languages
scope_note: Languages of the hands, face and body, used by Deaf communities worldwide.

label: Pidgins and creoles
scope_note: Languages that arose from contact between speakers of different languages.

label: Constructed languages
scope_note: Languages deliberately designed, such as Esperanto.

label: Writing systems and scripts
scope_note: The systems people use to write languages, classified by how their signs map to language.

label: Alphabets
scope_note: Scripts with separate letters for consonants and vowels, such as Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Georgian and Hangul.

label: Abjads
scope_note: Scripts that write mainly consonants, such as Arabic, Hebrew and Syriac.

label: Abugidas
scope_note: Scripts in which vowels are marked on consonant letters, such as Devanagari, Tamil, Thai and Ge'ez.

label: Syllabaries
scope_note: Scripts with signs for whole syllables, such as Japanese kana, Cherokee and Vai.

label: Logographic writing
scope_note: Writing in which signs stand for words or morphemes, as in Chinese characters, Egyptian hieroglyphs and Maya script.

label: Communication and media
scope_note: How people exchange information and meaning, and the media that carry it.

label: Journalism and news
scope_note: Gathering, verifying and reporting news.

label: Radio and television
scope_note: Radio and television, their technologies, institutions and programmes.

label: Social media
scope_note: Online platforms for sharing and discussion, and their social effects.

label: Advertising and public relations
scope_note: Persuasive communication on behalf of products, organizations and causes.

label: Propaganda and persuasion
scope_note: Communication designed to shape opinion, including disinformation, and how it is studied and countered.

label: Rhetoric
scope_note: The art and study of persuasive speech and writing.

label: Nonverbal communication
scope_note: Gesture, facial expression, posture and other communication without words.

label: Translation and interpreting
scope_note: Carrying meaning between languages in writing and speech.

label: Oral tradition
scope_note: Knowledge, history and art passed on by word of mouth across generations.

label: Books and publishing
scope_note: Producing and distributing books and other publications.

label: Semiotics
scope_note: Signs, symbols and how they produce meaning.
